newsitem.title: USA: Tribune CEO given raise in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Tribune CEO given raise in 1996.

text.p: John Madigan, chairman and chief executive officer of Tribune Co, was paid a salary of $728,000 in 1996, a four percent merit rise from 1995, according to a regulatory filing Wednesday.
In a proxy filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission, Tribune said Madigan's increase was effective as of February 28, 1996 when its financial performance was set.

Madigan's annual compensation overall for 1996 evened out to $724,231, up from $676,539 in 1995. The amount represents salary compensation for 52 weeks for fiscal years 1996 and 1994 and 53 weeks for fiscal 1995, The Tribune said.

For 1996, Tribune paid Madigan a bonus of $698,880, reflecting achievement of financial performance objectives, progress toward company-wide objectives and his individual performance and achievements.

In July 1996, the company awarded Madigan a non-qualified stock option (adjusted for the stock split) to buy 90,000 common shares at the current fair market value, which was then $34.81 per share. The options expire on August 30, 2006.
